title: Fix recency and expiry bugs in the LRU cache with TTL
prompt:
src/lru.mjs (an LRU cache with per-entry TTL and an injected clock) is evicting the wrong entries and keeps stale ones alive. Intended semantics:

- get(key) returns the value and marks the entry most-recently-used, but does NOT extend its expiry.
- has(key) reports presence without touching recency.
- set(key, value, { ttlMs }) inserts or overwrites; overwriting makes the entry most-recently-used and restarts its expiry. ttlMs per call overrides the cache default; a ttl of 0/undefined means never expires.
- An entry is expired once now >= insertedAt + ttl; expired entries are invisible to get/has/size/keys().
- When a set pushes the number of live entries above `max`, expired entries are dropped first and only then the least-recently-used live entry is evicted.
- size counts live entries; keys() lists live keys from most- to least-recently-used.

Fix the implementation; `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"` must pass.
